component.name: GFN Launcher
component.summary: Couch launcher for NVIDIA GeForce NOW

description.p: A console-like launcher for NVIDIA GeForce NOW. It runs fullscreen on a TV, is driven entirely by gamepad, starts with your desktop session, and hands games off to the GeForce NOW client you already have installed.

Built for the television rather than the desktop: a 10-foot interface you drive from three metres away, where the cover art is the brightest thing on screen and the launcher's own chrome gets out of the way.

ul.li: Browses the full GeForce NOW catalogue with genre and ray-tracing filters
Shows your library and what you own, once you sign in
Searches from an on-screen alphabetical keyboard, because on a pad you scan for a letter rather than reach for it
Keeps a chronology of what you played
Reports GeForce NOW service health, opening with your own datacenter rather than a list of seventy-six
Ends the session — sleep, restart, or turn off — because the launcher is the last thing on screen before the TV goes off

description.p: Requires the official GeForce NOW Flatpak, com.nvidia.geforcenow. An account is not needed to browse or to launch: the deep link goes to the local client. Signing in adds your library and ownership.
This is an unofficial, independent project, not affiliated with or endorsed by NVIDIA.

description.p: Bluetooth devices can now be paired from the launcher, without leaving it for the desktop.

ul.li: Settings has a Devices screen: what you have already paired, and what is in the room. Scan, press A on a row to pair it, again to connect or disconnect, X to forget
The pairing is the system's own — the launcher drives BlueZ the way your desktop's Bluetooth panel does — so a pad paired here works everywhere and comes back after a restart
Nearby devices are ordered by signal strength, so the one in your hand is at the top, and rows show a battery figure for the devices that report one
The on-screen keyboard in pointer mode moved from X to LB + RB, because with a cursor up the face buttons read as mouse buttons
A failed update no longer stretches its own dialog off the edge of the screen

description.p: The pad can now be a mouse and a keyboard, and a controller switched on before the launcher is recognised.

ul.li: Hold L3 + R3 and the pad becomes a mouse: the left stick moves a cursor, the right stick scrolls, A clicks and X opens an on-screen keyboard — so signing in to NVIDIA, which is not gamepad-navigable, no longer needs a keyboard

Optionally the same cursor works on the desktop and inside a running game, for a licence prompt or an updater that wants a click; off by default under Settings, and it asks the desktop for permission once
A gamepad switched on before the launcher starts is recognised straight away, instead of staying dead until it is unplugged and plugged back in
A stray mouse click can no longer reach the launcher sitting behind a running game
The keyboard shortcuts stop working while something else has the screen, matching what the pad already did

description.p: Fixes for input during a game, library sync, and keeping up with the GeForce NOW client.

ul.li: The pad no longer drives the launcher while a game is streaming, and a button still held when the game ends is not read as a fresh press
The launcher follows the GeForce NOW client while it runs — a client that updates, or a server location changed in the GeForce NOW app, is picked up without a restart
Refreshing every store library works instead of answering "sync refused (401)", and names the stores that still refuse
A second press of the menu button during a hand-off no longer ends the game that is starting
Stores that do not offer library sync are left out of a refresh rather than reported as an error
The screen stops being held awake as soon as another window takes the focus
The cursor no longer moves inside a panel that is closing
Gamepad-only 10-foot interface with spatial focus navigation, recognising Xbox, PlayStation and 8BitDo pads and redrawing its button legend to match
The full GeForce NOW catalogue, with genre filtering, a ray-tracing filter and server-side search
Your library and store ownership once signed in, including which store's edition launches
A details panel with description, screenshots, supported controls and a QR code for the store page
GeForce NOW closed for you when a game ends, and the launcher raised back to the front
Service health, opening with your own datacenter
Accent colour, interface scale, autostart and a power menu
A support screen carrying a QR code for the donation page, scannable from a sofa
The screen kept awake while the pad is in use, which a desktop's idle timer does not do on its own
New versions found, installed and restarted into, wherever this build is allowed to replace itself
A log file with credentials stripped from it, ready to attach to a bug report
A crash screen that names the fault instead of leaving a black screen on the television
